title: Accounting Standard 17 Segment Reporting
outcomes: Explain the purpose of segment reporting and identify business and geographical segments.
Apply the 10% and 75% tests to identify reportable segments.
Measure segment results and state the required disclosures.

meta.exam_tip: For the result test, compute total profits and total losses separately and take 10% of the larger.

concepts.title: Purpose and scope of segment reporting
body: AS 17 asks an enterprise with several products, services or regions to report information by segment, so users can judge the different risks and returns that a single set of totals hides.

It applies where consolidated and separate statements are presented: segment information is given on the basis of the consolidated statements. Smaller enterprises (SMCs and non-Level I entities) are exempt.
concepts.analogy: Totals can hide a sick business inside a healthy group.
concepts.work: A firm selling both cement and software faces very different risks in each.

concepts.title: Business and geographical segments; primary and secondary formats
body: A business segment is a distinguishable component providing a product or service (or a group of related ones) with risks and returns different from other components; factors include nature of products, production processes, type of customers, distribution methods and regulatory environment.
A geographical segment provides products or services within a particular economic environment with different risks and returns — based on location of assets or of customers.

The dominant source of risks and returns decides the primary format (business or geographical); the other is secondary. The internal organisation and management reporting structure is usually the guide.
concepts.analogy: Primary format follows what drives risk most; the internal reports usually show it.
concepts.work: An exporter whose margins swing with each country's currency may choose geography as primary.

concepts.title: The 10% thresholds and the 75% test
body: A business or geographical segment is reportable if a majority of its revenue is from external customers and any one of these is 10% or more: its revenue (external and inter-segment) of total segment revenue; its result (profit or loss) of the larger of combined profits of profit-making segments or combined losses of loss-making segments; or its assets of total segment assets.
If reportable segments' external revenue is less than 75% of total enterprise revenue, more segments are added until 75% is reached, even if below 10%.

A segment reportable last year because it crossed a threshold continues to be reported this year if management judges it of continuing significance. Segments may also be reported voluntarily or combined if similar.
concepts.analogy: Any one 10% test is enough; then top up to 75%.
concepts.work: A segment with 6% of revenue but 15% of assets is reportable.

concepts.title: Segment revenue, expense, result, assets and liabilities
body: Segment revenue includes external and inter-segment sales directly attributable or reasonably allocable; it excludes extraordinary items, interest or dividend income (unless the segment's operations are financial) and gains on sale of investments.

Segment expense is directly attributable or reasonably allocable operating expense; it excludes interest expense (unless financial), losses on investments, income tax, extraordinary items and general administrative expenses relating to the enterprise as a whole.
Segment result = segment revenue − segment expense. Segment assets and liabilities are operating items used by, or arising from, the segment's operations; assets include allocable shared assets.
Segment information follows the same accounting policies as the financial statements.
concepts.analogy: Segment result is an operating figure before finance costs and tax.
concepts.work: Interest on a general corporate loan is not charged to a segment's result.

concepts.title: Disclosures for primary and secondary segments
body: Primary segments: segment revenue (external and inter-segment separately), segment result, carrying amount of segment assets, segment liabilities, capital expenditure, depreciation and amortisation, and significant non-cash expenses other than depreciation. A reconciliation to enterprise totals is given.
Secondary segments: revenue from external customers, carrying amount of assets and capital expenditure, for each segment above 10% of the relevant totals.

Also disclose the types of products and services in each business segment, the composition of each geographical segment, the basis of inter-segment pricing and any changes in it, and changes in segment accounting policies.
concepts.analogy: Primary gets the full picture; secondary gets the outline.
concepts.work: If business is primary, geography gets only revenue, assets and capex.

jobs.title: Testing segments for the annual report
jobs.situation: Management reports seven product lines internally and asks which must appear in the segment note.
steps: Confirm majority external revenue for each line.
jobs.takeaway: Work the tests systematically and document why a line is or is not reported.

mcqs.q: The primary reporting format for segments is decided by:
options: The dominant source and nature of risks and returns
mcqs.explain: AS 17 says the dominant source and nature of risks and returns governs whether business or geographical segments are primary; the internal organisation and management reporting structure normally indicate it. In practice: look at what management reviews.
mcqs.topic: Business and geographical segments; primary and secondary formats

mcqs.q: A segment is reportable if its revenue (external and inter-segment) is at least what share of total segment revenue?
mcqs.explain: One of the three tests is revenue of 10% or more of total revenue of all segments, counting both external and inter-segment sales. The other two tests use result and assets. In practice: one test is enough.

mcqs.q: Reportable segments' external revenue must reach at least what share of enterprise revenue?
mcqs.explain: If reportable segments account for less than 75% of total enterprise revenue, further segments are identified as reportable until that level is reached, even if they fail the 10% tests. In practice: add the next-largest segments.

mcqs.q: Combined profits of profit-making segments ₹300 lakh; combined losses ₹420 lakh. The result threshold is:
mcqs.explain: The result test uses 10% of the greater of combined profits or combined losses in absolute amount: the larger is ₹420 lakh, so the threshold is ₹42 lakh. In practice: compare each segment's result, ignoring sign.

mcqs.q: A segment with 7% of revenue, 4% of result and 12% of assets is:
options: Reportable only in the secondary format
mcqs.explain: Meeting any one of the three 10% tests makes a segment reportable, provided most of its revenue is external. Here the asset test is met at 12%. In practice: check all three tests.

mcqs.q: Which is excluded from segment expense?
mcqs.explain: Segment expense excludes income tax, interest (unless the segment is financial), losses on investments, extraordinary items and general enterprise-level administration costs. Direct and allocable operating costs are included. In practice: segment result is pre-tax.
mcqs.topic: Segment revenue, expense, result, assets and liabilities

mcqs.q: Interest income is included in segment revenue only when:
options: The segment's operations are primarily financial
It is from a related party
mcqs.explain: Interest and dividend income are generally kept out of segment revenue; the exception is a segment whose business is mainly financial, such as lending. In practice: treat a finance arm differently.
mcqs.topic: Segment revenue, expense, result, assets and liabilities

mcqs.q: Which disclosure is required for secondary segments?
options: Revenue from external customers, assets and capital expenditure
mcqs.explain: For the secondary format AS 17 requires only revenue from external customers, carrying amount of segment assets and additions to fixed assets for segments over the 10% levels. The primary format carries the fuller list. In practice: keep secondary notes brief.
mcqs.topic: Disclosures for primary and secondary segments

options: The same accounting policies as the financial statements
Policies chosen for internal reporting only
mcqs.explain: AS 17 requires segment information to follow the accounting policies adopted for the enterprise's financial statements, so it reconciles with the totals. In practice: adjust internal reports where policies differ.
mcqs.topic: Segment revenue, expense, result, assets and liabilities

mcqs.q: A segment reported last year falls below all thresholds this year. It:
options: Continues to be reported if management judges it of continuing significance
mcqs.explain: If a segment was reportable in the previous period, it continues to be reported in the current period, despite falling below the thresholds, when management judges it to be of continuing significance. In practice: explain the judgement.

summary: Business or geographical segments; primary format follows dominant risks.
Reportable: majority external revenue + any 10% test (revenue, result, assets).
Top up to 75% of enterprise revenue.
Segment result excludes interest, tax, corporate costs.
Primary: full disclosures with reconciliation; secondary: revenue, assets, capex.
remember: Continuing significance keeps last year's segment.
traps: Result test uses the larger of profits or losses, not the net.

viva.model: A distinguishable component of an enterprise that provides a product or service, or group of related ones, and is subject to risks and returns different from other components.
Revenue, result, or assets of the segment being 10% or more of the respective totals — with the result test measured against the larger of total profits or total losses.
If reportable segments' external revenue is below 75% of total enterprise revenue, more segments are identified as reportable until 75% is covered.

viva.q: What items are excluded from segment expense?
viva.model: Interest expense unless the segment is financial, losses on investments, income tax, extraordinary items and general corporate administrative costs.

viva.q: What does the secondary format disclose?
viva.model: Revenue from external customers, carrying amount of segment assets and capital expenditure for each significant secondary segment.

cases.title: Nirmala Group
cases.case: Nirmala Ltd. has segments Textiles (revenue ₹520 crore, 95% external), Chemicals (₹380 crore, 40% external — mostly supplied to Textiles), and Retail (₹100 crore, all external). Its risks vary mainly with products; internal reports are by product line.

mcqs.q: The primary format for Nirmala is:
mcqs.explain: Risks and returns vary mainly with products, and internal reports are by product line, so business segments form the primary format and geography secondary. In practice: document the basis.
mcqs.topic: Business and geographical segments; primary and secondary formats

mcqs.q: Chemicals, with only 40% external revenue, is:
options: Not separately reportable, as most of its revenue is not from external customers
mcqs.explain: A segment is reportable only if a majority of its revenue comes from external customers and it meets a 10% test. Chemicals sells mostly within the group, so it fails the first condition. In practice: it may be reported voluntarily.

mcqs.q: Retail's share of total segment revenue is:
mcqs.explain: Total segment revenue is ₹520 + 380 + 100 = ₹1,000 crore, so Retail's ₹100 crore is 10%, exactly meeting the revenue test. In practice: the test is "10% or more".
